clue.text: A strapless top is a mistake on the Underground

parts.note: a boob is a silly blunder
the Tube is London's Underground railway

explanation.surface: A wardrobe malfunction with a strapless top happens on a crowded London train.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tube is the everyday name for the London Underground.
explanation.definitionFit: A boob tube is the British name for a tight elasticated garment worn round the chest without shoulder straps.

clue.text: Worker provides assistance

explanation.surface: An employee helps out.
explanation.definitionFit: A hired labourer is a hand, and giving someone a hand means helping them with a task.

clue.text: Potency of port half an hour later

indicators.note: only part of the word for sixty minutes is kept, its opening letter being dropped

parts.note: Vigo is a port in north-west Spain
the unit of time, taken as written

explanation.surface: Port wine is said to grow stronger if left for another thirty minutes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'later' puts the hour piece after the port; of its four letters only the second half is kept.
explanation.definitionFit: Vigour means strength, energy and force, which is what potency describes.

clue.text: Old man's period for diversion

parts.note: pa is father, the old man, with the possessive S
a period is a stretch of time

explanation.surface: Dad's spare hours are set aside for some amusement.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastime is a hobby or recreation, something done to amuse or entertain oneself.

clue.text: Godly foe disposed to be reactionary

indicators.note: to dispose is to arrange or set out, so the letters are laid out afresh

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: An enemy of the devout turns out to be conservative in outlook.
explanation.definitionFit: An old fogey is a person with stuffy, old-fashioned views who resists change, much like a reactionary.

clue.text: In error, since I'm not all-knowing

indicators.note: something in error is wrong, so these letters are in the wrong order

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A modest admission: I could be wrong, because I don't know everything.
explanation.definitionFit: Omniscient describes someone with complete, unlimited understanding of every matter.

clue.text: She may out pantihose, but not net

indicators.note: out suggests something put out of order, so the remaining letters are jumbled
these words tell us to take some letters away from the hosiery word

parts.note: the hosiery word, taken as written
these three letters are removed

explanation.surface: A woman might go out in tights, though not fishnet ones.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove N, E and T from PANTIHOSE to leave PAIHOS, then shuffle to get the girl's name SOPHIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Sophia is a woman's name, so a female person could be one, as 'she' indicates.

clue.text: Reproduction of a man's oil painting

indicators.note: a reproduction is a remade copy, so the letters are made up again in a new order

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A print copy of some fellow's oil painting.
explanation.walkthrough: Reproductions of Leonardo's portrait are everywhere, which makes the surface apt.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mona Lisa is Leonardo da Vinci's famous portrait, hanging in the Louvre, an example of a painting.

clue.text: Lemons and melons may come from here

definitions.text: Lemons and melons may come from here

parts.words: Lemons and melons may come from here
parts.note: surface reading: a place where these fruits are grown
setter's reading: both words can be produced by rearranging the letters of a Greek island's name

explanation.surface: Somewhere sunny that grows citrus and melons.
explanation.walkthrough: LEMNOS, a Greek island in the Aegean, rearranges to both LEMONS and MELONS, so the fruits literally come from its letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Lemnos is a Greek island whose warm climate suits fruit growing, and whose letters spell both fruits.

clue.text: Lincoln died sleeping? Apparently so

parts.note: Abe is Abraham Lincoln's familiar first name
d is the standard abbreviation for died

explanation.surface: Did Abraham Lincoln pass away in his sleep?
explanation.walkthrough: Lincoln was in fact shot at a theatre, which is why the question is only 'apparently' so.
explanation.definitionFit: Abed means in bed, so someone abed is lying down and probably sleeping.

clue.text: Proverbially it implies madness

parts.note: surface reading: some saying links a thing to insanity
setter's reading: the proverb continues 'out of mind', and being out of one's mind is madness

explanation.walkthrough: The proverb is 'out of sight, out of mind'; the answer is its first half, which by the saying brings on the second.
explanation.definitionFit: The saying pairs being unseen with being forgotten, and 'out of one's mind' also means insane.

clue.text: Tugboat?

parts.note: surface reading: a small vessel that tows ships
setter's reading: a boat whose name sounds like someone who hauls or drags things

explanation.walkthrough: To lug is to tug or haul, so a vessel whose name reads as 'one who lugs' is literally a tug boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A lugger is a small sailing vessel with lugsails, and lugging means dragging heavily, just like tugging.

clue.text: Was it designed for handicapped drivers?

definitions.text: Was it designed for handicapped drivers?

parts.note: surface reading: motorists with a disability
setter's reading: players with a handicap who hit drivers, the long-distance clubs

explanation.walkthrough: A driver is also a golf club, and golfers play off a handicap.
explanation.definitionFit: A golf course is laid out for golfers, who carry drivers and have handicaps measuring their ability.

clue.text: Christmas visitors can include one conjuror

parts.note: the Magi, or Wise Men, visited the infant Jesus at the Nativity

indicators.note: to include something is to take it inside, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Among the festive guests there may be an entertainer doing tricks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can' looks like a verb but is the container, with I put after its C.
explanation.definitionFit: A magician is a conjuror, a performer of sleight-of-hand and illusion tricks.

clue.text: Lose wind when seeking muddy shoal in Cheshire estuary

indicators.note: in places one item inside the letters of the river name

parts.note: the River Dee meets the sea in an estuary on Cheshire's border with Wales
a flat, as in mudflat, is a stretch of shallow muddy ground

explanation.surface: A walker grows breathless while hunting for mudbanks in a river mouth.
explanation.walkthrough: Cheshire is an English county in the north-west; the Dee is its river.
explanation.definitionFit: To deflate is to let air out, as a tyre or balloon loses its wind.

clue.text: Music of the Depression?

parts.note: surface reading: songs from the 1930s economic slump
setter's reading: low spirits, and the musical genre named for that sad feeling

explanation.walkthrough: The capital D suggests the Great Depression, but the clue means gloominess.
explanation.definitionFit: The blues is a melancholy African-American musical genre, and 'the blues' also means feeling sad.

clue.text: The sort ready to compose something impressive?

parts.note: a type is a sort or kind
set means prepared, ready to go

explanation.surface: The kind of person all prepared to write some masterpiece.
explanation.walkthrough: In printing, composing means setting type, and type makes impressions on paper.
explanation.definitionFit: To typeset is to arrange printing type, which compositors do so that it presses an image onto the page.

clue.text: Charm one's way in

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to delight or put into a trance, a verb stressed on the second syllable
second meaning: a door or gateway, a noun stressed on the first syllable

explanation.surface: Using charm to get through the door.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to bewitch or captivate; as a noun it is a doorway or point of access.

clue.text: Possibly spy on fashionable medium

indicators.note: possibly signals that the word may take another form, so its letters are moved about

parts.note: the letters rearranged
chic means stylish

explanation.surface: Perhaps an agent keeps watch on a stylish spiritualist.
explanation.definitionFit: A medium claims to contact spirits of the dead, so is a person with supposed supernatural powers.

clue.text: Nuts? You'll need these

definitions.meaning: second meaning: tools for opening the nuts just mentioned, nutcrackers

explanation.walkthrough: Read the clue as a question about nuts to eat and the second half needs nutcrackers; but 'nuts' also means mad.
explanation.definitionFit: Crackers is British slang for insane, and crackers are also the implements that split nutshells.

clue.text: Smoking jacket?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: something smoked, a cannabis cigarette
second meaning: a short thick double-breasted coat worn by sailors

explanation.walkthrough: 'Smoking jacket' looks like one item of clothing, but it splits into two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A reefer is slang for a marijuana joint, and a reefer jacket is a heavy naval-style coat.

clue.text: Property gets one thousand short of estimate

indicators.note: short of means lacking, so the given items are taken away

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: A house sale fetches a thousand pounds less than the valuation.
explanation.walkthrough: Take I and M out of ESTIMATE to leave ESTATE.
explanation.definitionFit: An estate is land or possessions owned by someone, which is property.

clue.text: Hemingway or Sterne, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the surname could be rearranged into something else

parts.note: the letters to rearrange; Laurence Sterne wrote Tristram Shandy

explanation.surface: Two novelists, Hemingway and Sterne, are offered as examples.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue pretends to want a writer's surname; it wants Hemingway's first name, which also fits Sterne's letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Ernest Hemingway was the American author of The Old Man and the Sea; his given name was Ernest.

clue.text: He's against accepting royalties

parts.note: surface reading: refusing to take payments for a book or song
setter's reading: royal persons, so someone opposed to having a monarchy

explanation.walkthrough: Royalties suggests an author's earnings, but here it means members of a royal family.
explanation.definitionFit: A republican wants a state with an elected head instead of a king or queen.

clue.text: A mother for the first orphan?

parts.note: taken as written
a dam is the mother of an animal, especially a horse

explanation.surface: Seeking a mother to adopt the earliest parentless child.
explanation.walkthrough: Adam, the first man in Genesis, was created without parents, so he was in a sense an orphan.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical first human had no father or mother, hence the playful question-marked description.

clue.text: Just open — so have a glass of ale

definitions.meaning: first meaning: of a door, slightly open
second meaning: a jar is British slang for a pint of beer

explanation.surface: The pub has only just opened its doors, so let's have a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang, going for 'a jar' means having a pint of beer.
explanation.definitionFit: A door that is ajar stands slightly open, and 'a jar' is colloquial for a beer.

clue.text: Tenant in the French diocese

parts.note: les is the French plural article
a see is a bishop's diocese

explanation.surface: Someone renting a home within a French bishop's region.
explanation.definitionFit: A lessee holds property under a lease, paying rent to the owner as a tenant does.

clue.text: Example set by the ancients, maybe

indicators.note: maybe hints the word could appear in some other form, so it is rearranged

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A model left for us by the people of antiquity.
explanation.definitionFit: An instance is a single case or illustration of something, which is what an example is.
